operations.text: 0.3.16 writes into the doctrine the rules the loop had been carrying as recorded gaps or as local habits. In ORCHESTRATOR.md: a question the operator must answer is a dialog, the new rule 9 of the section on how the COO speaks to the operator - the harness's question tool (AskUserQuestion in Claude Code), one topic, numbered options with the consequence of each, the recommendation first, in words and counts and never with line numbers, up to four points, what does not block the ticket in one dialog at its end, never a list in the chat - and an operator's own question is answered directly, never turned into a dialog; an agent, a check or a pass the doctrine does not require and the ticket does not name is written into the ticket with its scope and cost before it is spent, while the scan-tier work the doctrine does require rides the ticket's word; the exempt list that closes an enumeration names non-callers only, never a caller by its purpose; a change after which the user sees less than before - a field, a row or a function gone - stops the ticket for the operator's word; a later remark in which the operator takes a step themselves narrows the standing word to what precedes that step, and the COO waits there for the next word; when a word names no tree, the session's own project root is the tree; the discovery scan records the baseline-red tests by name and the Writer brief carries that expected red set. In work.md: the R3 class covers schema or data migrations of the product's persistent store, and a plugin's payload migration routes by its diff; the four COO routing checks are read after the discovery scan, so a scan that anchors every item answers check 2 with no; for a ticket whose brief says E2E: yes the COO runs the E2E spec at the handoff, before the code audit, and the routes show that step. In ticket.md: the brief carries two new lines, E2E: yes | no - because <reason> and Escalation: none | trigger <N> - <why>, and its Verify line names the expected red set; the live Writer is resumed with a message to the dispatched agent (SendMessage in Claude Code) for every micro-round, every correction round and the commit, a fresh spawn only when that agent has ended; the CHANGELOG is kept in the language the project's CLAUDE.md Changelog format section names, and the operator's quotes are never translated; a ticket whose outcome is visible in the running product may close on its offline proof when the operator declines their own run in words, the waiver quoted and the outcome marked as not seen by the operator; a roadmap entry or finding line carries the problem, its evidence, the operator's words and the scope, never the fix, and a nested list's parent line closes with its last child, each line against the record or commit that closes it, never as a sweep. In plan.md: a second readiness pass needs a BLOCKER that reverses a decision the operator made - a D-NN carrying the operator's words or a dialog answer - and a BLOCKER that reverses a COO decision is a revision, never a second pass. The managed CLAUDE.md region shows the E2E run in the R2 route, and the Writer agent carries the same CHANGELOG-language clause, since the Writer writes the release's block. In the payload documents: the readiness corpus gains class 17 (the NULL case of a boolean predicate) and class 18 (a replaced reader), and the templates contract says a rule names the property it checks, not a list of kinds of work. Two seeds changed as well - the overrides document's line on the second readiness pass and the roadmap template's quote form - and a seed is written once, so this update reaches no installed copy of either: reword yours on your operator's word if you want the new form. This update re-renders ORCHESTRATOR.md, work.md, ticket.md, plan.md, the Writer agent and the managed CLAUDE.md region; every additions block is carried. An overrides document that carries its own rule that a question to the operator is a dialog may delete it on its operator's word: the core now carries that rule as rule 9. If this release introduces a word-gate: check your local rules for self-initiated dispatch or remediation - a rule written before this gate may contradict it.
